[[Category:Legal entity]]
In law, a '''minor person''' is a person considered less capable of exercising their legal rights and assuming their legal obligations by law in virtue of their young age.<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>

== Age of majority ==

The '''age of majority''' is the minimum legal age a person must have to be considered '''adult''', i.e., person ordinarily capable of understanding and participating in legal processes independently.

In many [[jurisdiction]]s, the age of majority is '''18 years'''.

Persons who have not yet attained the age of majority are therefore considered '''minors'''.

== Legal status ==

=== Representation ===

In most [[jurisdiction]]s, '''minors''' are legally '''represented by their [[legal guardian]]s.

==== Exception ====

In some [[jurisdiction]]s, however, '''minors''' can exercise certain legal rights alone.

In France, for example, a minor does not require parental approval to

* consent to medical treatment, if the medical professional proposing it considers the minor reasonably capable of understanding the treatment and its consequences.<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>
